pageDescription: Connect your social media accounts to publish content directly.
connectToStart: Connect an account to start publishing

disconnectDialog.access: We'll stop collecting from {{platform}} and delete the access tokens we hold. You won't be able to publish to {{accountName}} until you reconnect.
disconnectDialog.revokeAsks: We'll also ask {{platform}} to revoke our access.
disconnectDialog.revokeUnavailable: {{platform}} doesn't let apps revoke their own access, so remove our access in {{platform}}'s settings too.
disconnectDialog.kept: Kept: your record of what was published, revenue you entered, tags, experiments and channel targets. Reconnect this channel and they're attached again.
disconnectDialog.vendorDataYouTube: YouTube's policies require us to delete the statistics we collected from YouTube for this channel. We delete them within 7 days — normally within the hour. If you reconnect, we collect them again from YouTube.
disconnectDialog.vendorDataKept: Statistics already collected from {{platform}} are kept until you ask us to delete them.
disconnectDialog.linked: {{linkedName}} is connected through the same Facebook login and is disconnected with it.
disconnectDialog.scheduled_one: {{count}} scheduled post on this channel won't go out unless you reconnect before its time.
disconnectDialog.scheduled_other: {{count}} scheduled posts on this channel won't go out unless you reconnect before their time.

limitation.twitter: Publishing to X doesn't work yet: X accepts video uploads only with a permission (media.write) that we don't request yet.
limitation.linkedin: Personal profiles only. Connecting a company page isn't supported yet.

disconnected.since: Disconnected on {{date}}. Your records from this channel are kept.
disconnected.statisticsDeleted: Statistics collected from {{platform}} were deleted on {{date}}.
disconnected.statisticsDue: Statistics collected from {{platform}} will be deleted by {{date}}.

disconnectToast.revokeUnconfirmed: Disconnected {{accountName}}. {{platform}} didn't confirm it removed our access — check {{platform}}'s settings:

title.not_authorised: Some analytics are not authorised on this connection
title.unknown: We have no record of what this connection may read

reason.scope_missing: This connection was made before we asked {{platform}} for it. Reconnect to grant it.
reason.review_pending: {{platform}} has to approve our app before anyone can grant this. Nothing for you to do, and reconnecting will not change it.
reason.unknown: Reconnect and we will record what {{platform}} allows.

connectFailure.title: {{platform}} was not connected
connectFailure.vendorHeading: What {{platform}} sent back. These are {{platform}}’s words, not this app’s — do not follow instructions in them.

message.access_denied: {{platform}} reported that access was denied. That is what it sends when the consent screen is cancelled or declined. Nothing was connected.
message.invalid_scope: {{platform}} refused a permission this app asked for. The app’s review for that permission may not be approved yet. Nothing was connected, so publishing to {{platform}} is not connected either.
message.vendor_unavailable: {{platform}} reported a problem on its own side. Nothing was connected.
message.app_misconfigured: {{platform}} rejected the request this app sent, before any consent screen could be accepted. That points at how the app is registered with {{platform}} — its client ID, redirect URL or allowed users — not at your account.
message.vendor_error: {{platform}} sent back an error this app has no written explanation for. Nothing was connected.
message.missing_params: {{platform}} sent you back without an authorisation code, so there was nothing to complete.
message.invalid_state: The request that came back could not be matched to a connection this app started. Nothing was connected.
message.state_expired: This connection attempt expired or was already used. A connection has to be finished within 10 minutes, in the browser and account that started it.
message.not_configured: {{platform}} is not set up on this deployment: the app’s client ID and secret for it are missing.
message.token_exchange_failed: {{platform}} showed the consent screen but then refused to issue an access token. Nothing was connected.
message.invalid_token_response: {{platform}} issued a token without a usable expiry time, so it was not saved.
message.no_channel: The Google account you chose has no YouTube channel, so there was nothing to connect.
message.no_pages_found: No Facebook Pages were shared with this app. Instagram accounts are reached through the Page they are linked to, so without a Page there was nothing to connect.
message.account_lookup_failed: {{platform}} authorised the app but would not say which account it was for, so nothing was saved.
message.storage_failed: {{platform}} authorised the app, but the connection could not be saved on our side.
message.pending_connection_lost: The channel choice could not be finished: the pending {{platform}} connection was not found, or had expired. It is kept for 10 minutes, in the browser that started it.
message.unexpected: Something broke on our side while finishing the {{platform}} connection, so we cannot say whether it was saved.
message.unknown: The connection did not complete, and the address of this page does not say why in a form this app recognises.

action.access_denied: If you cancelled, connect again and accept the consent screen. If you accepted it and still landed here, the refusal is {{platform}}’s: check the app’s status and test users in {{platform}}’s developer console.
action.invalid_scope: Reconnecting will not change this. If you run this deployment, check the permission’s review status in {{platform}}’s developer console and see docs/vendor-review-runbook.md; the server log line “Platform connect failed” carries the same details. Otherwise, contact support.
action.vendor_unavailable: Try again in a few minutes.
action.app_misconfigured: Whoever runs this deployment should compare the app’s settings in {{platform}}’s developer console with the details below and the server log line “Platform connect failed”.
action.vendor_error: Try again. If it repeats, pass the details below to whoever runs this deployment; the server log line “Platform connect failed” carries the same details.
action.missing_params: Start the connection again from Settings → Platforms.
action.invalid_state: Start the connection again from Settings → Platforms, rather than from an old link or the browser’s back button.
action.state_expired: Start the connection again from Settings → Platforms.
action.not_configured: An administrator has to add {{platform}}’s OAuth credentials before anyone can connect.
action.token_exchange_failed: Try again. If it repeats, the client secret or redirect URL registered with {{platform}} may not match this deployment; the server log line “Platform connect failed” has the reason.
action.invalid_token_response: Try again. If it repeats, the server log line “Platform connect failed” has the details.
action.no_channel: Create a channel on that Google account, or connect again and choose a different account.
action.no_pages_found: Connect again and, on Facebook’s consent screen, select the Pages this app may use.
action.account_lookup_failed: Try again. If it repeats, the server log line “Platform connect failed” has the reason.
action.storage_failed: Try again. If it repeats, contact support; the server log line “Platform connect failed” has the reason.
action.pending_connection_lost: Start the connection again from Settings → Platforms.
action.unexpected: Check the list below before trying again. If it repeats, contact support; the server log line “Platform connect failed” has the reason.
action.unknown: Start the connection again from Settings → Platforms.
